Abstract

Huh7 cells were exposed to BNT162b2, and quantitative PCR was performed on RNA extracted from the cells. We detected high levels of BNT162b2 in Huh7 cells and changes in gene expression of long interspersed nuclear element-1 (LINE-1), which is an endogenous reverse transcriptase. Maternal COVID-19 Vaccination and Prevention of Symptomatic Infection in Infants

A study conducted by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) reveals that pregnant women receiving mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines can pass strong protection against symptomatic COVID-19 to their infants for at least six months after birth. Published in Pediatrics, the study emphasizes the significance of pregnant women receiving both vaccination and booster shots to ensure infants are born with lasting protection until they can be vaccinated.

Newborns and young infants are especially vulnerable to COVID-19, lacking available vaccines for those under six months old. Previous findings from the Multisite Observational Maternal and Infant COVID-19 Vaccine (MOMI-Vax) study showed antibodies from maternal vaccination present in newborns' cord blood, suggesting potential protection. However, the duration and effectiveness of this protection remained unknown.

In this segment of the MOMI-Vax study, data from 475 infants born to vaccinated mothers were analyzed. Of these, 271 infants were born to mothers who received two doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines during pregnancy, while 204 were born to mothers who also received a booster shot. Infants were evaluated during follow-up visits in their first six months after birth, with parents reporting any COVID-19 infections or symptoms.

Results indicated that newborns with high antibody levels at birth had greater protection against COVID-19 in their first six months. Infants born to mothers who received a booster shot during pregnancy exhibited higher antibody levels at birth and increased protection against COVID-19 during follow-up visits.

Although older individuals should adhere to CDC guidelines for COVID-19 vaccination, this study underscores the benefits of maternal vaccination for newborns too young to receive the vaccine. Notably, none of the infants studied required hospitalization for COVID-19 during the research period. Ongoing evaluation of MOMI-Vax study data will provide further insights into COVID-19 protection in infants. https://t.co/G8OShNJgf3
